script: I'd skip my dad's kids, but babysitting my niece exposed a dark secret.. I am 34, my sister 37, and she has a three‑year‑old. We used to be like two weird sisters, but when she announced she was pregnant, I thought we'd finally bond. Nope. The opposite. We got closer than ever. Now I love that kid like I love a super‑rare Pokémon. I babysit her every other weekend just so I can be that "nice aunt" she deserves. Babysitting is a huge favor, so I only do it for people I actually care about. Now my dad's girlfriend is the same age as me. She's got a two‑year‑old and a newborn. She's my dad's new girl, not my sister. The whole dynamic feels like a bad joke. My dad's kids remind me of the trauma I had growing up—abandonment, physical punishment, that whole mess. I've been in therapy for years. When she told me she was pregnant, I said "cool" but it didn't feel like the joy I felt for my sister's baby. I am polite to her and the kids, but I don't love them. They're not my responsibility. So my dad asks me to watch their kids for an evening so they can go on a date. He asks while the girlfriend is there. I say no. She asks why I treat "my siblings" differently than my niece. I am like, "you're not my sister. These kids are not my kids. Babysitting is a gift. I choose who gets it." I explain that my niece brings happiness, her kids bring up my trauma. I am not handing out free childcare because I am a saint. She screams about how I need to act like an adult and let go of the past. I tell her I'll never babysit them and walk out. Then my dad calls, furious, saying the kids are my siblings and I should bond with them. I am like, "I am old enough to be their aunt. They're younger than my niece. We didn't grow up together. My life was poverty and abuse; theirs is abundance and safety." I don't want to be stuck in that loop, watching my dad try to fix what he never fixed for me. So, am I the jerk for not babysitting my dad's kids while I do my sister's? I don't know. I am not a child person. I am not a martyr. I am just not going to drag myself into someone else's past just to play a role. I've got my own trauma to heal. I am better than them in the sense that I've survived. If I can't be the hero, I am not the villain.
